lines.text: Cloud analytics can feel like a wall of product names. Before Fabric, you need a simple model: who owns the service, where your
organization lives, where teams work, what provides compute and where analytical items/data are organized.
Explain cloud responsibility at a beginner level; distinguish tenant, workspace, capacity and item; recognize Fabric as SaaS and avoid
C2-06 workload/warehouse concepts help, but no Azure administration experience is assumed.
5. New words before we use them
SaaS: Software delivered and operated as a managed service; you use/configure it rather than managing all infrastructure. Tenant: Organization-level
boundary for identities, settings and Fabric/Power BI environment. Capacity: Allocated compute resources used by Fabric workloads; separate concept from
VISUAL/SOURCE ROUTE: Microsoft Fabric overview is required visual/reference. Trial is optional and never required for mastery.
After watching/opening: return to this lesson and reproduce the worked example from your own file/query/report. Save course-task evidence, not a screenshot of the
Apartment utility model: the organization/tenant owns the environment and identities; workspaces organize team content; capacity supplies managed
compute; items/data are the things teams build and govern. Cloud removes infrastructure chores, not ownership, security, cost or validation
Teacher demonstration - do this once with me, then close the example before your fresh task.
Business asks for governed Sales analytics used by 200 employees. Start with the organization/tenant-not with a VM.
Create a conceptual Analytics workspace for team-owned Fabric/Power BI items. A workspace is a collaboration/security boundary inside the
Place a semantic model/report and, if needed, a lakehouse/warehouse/pipeline inside the workspace.
Capacity supplies compute for Fabric workloads; identity and tenant policies control who can use/create items. OneLake is Fabric's unified
logical data lake, not the same thing as capacity.
Write which responsibilities remain with Microsoft (managed service/infrastructure) versus your organization (access, data, workspace design,
8. What you should see / be able to say
You can place tenant -> workspace -> items and explain capacity/identity responsibilities without Azure-infrastructure jargon.
The mental model separates organization, collaboration boundary, compute and data/items instead of treating 'cloud' as one box. Professional upgrade:
Fabric is currently delivered as SaaS, and Fabric tenants automatically include OneLake. Capacity sizing/licensing can change, so this course teaches
responsibilities and boundaries before SKU memorization.
1. Tenant = workspace. | 2. Capacity = storage folder. | 3. Cloud removes responsibility for permissions/governance. | 4. Assuming Fabric
requires you to provision Azure resource groups for ordinary use.
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
Draw four labeled boxes only: Organization/Tenant -> Workspace -> Items, with Capacity beside them as compute. Add OneLake as shared storage
foundation. Save the genuine attempt before review.
12. Now you do a small version alone
Fresh case: a retail company needs Finance and Operations analytics with separate ownership but some shared certified data. Sketch
Your diagram names owners, access boundary, compute boundary and shared-data path; no product term is used without a job.
14. Teach it back in your own words
Explain tenant, workspace and capacity to a manager using organization -> team room -> engine.
Save first diagram. Changed retry uses a consulting company with two client workspaces and a central governed semantic-model team.
Cloud responsibility matrix + tenant/workspace/capacity/item diagram + explain-back. After saving evidence, continue to CLD2.
CLD2 - Compute, storage and identity concepts
Most enterprise incidents happen because someone confuses 'can the engine run?' with 'is this user allowed?' or 'where does the data
live?'. Compute, storage and identity are separate control planes.
Distinguish compute, storage and identity; apply least privilege to people/groups/service principals conceptually; explain why a job may have
compute but still fail due to data/credential permission.
5. New words before we use them
Compute: Resources that execute queries, refreshes, pipelines or notebooks. Identity: User, group or application/service principal that requests access.
Least privilege: Grant only the minimum permissions needed for the intended job, for the required scope/time.
VISUAL/SOURCE ROUTE: Book-led; current workspace-role and Fabric overview references are enough.
After watching/opening: return to this lesson and reproduce the worked example from your own file/query/report. Save course-task evidence, not a screenshot of the
Kitchen model: storage is the pantry that keeps ingredients, compute is the stove that performs work, and identity is the keycard that decides who may
enter and use each resource. Data can persist when compute stops, and available compute does not override access policy.
Teacher demonstration - do this once with me, then close the example before your fresh task.
Capacity is available: the service has compute to run a semantic-model refresh.
Refresh identity/connection still needs permission and valid credentials to reach its data source.
The workspace role controls what a person/service principal can do with Fabric/Power BI items, but source-system permission can be separate.
OneLake/item permissions and semantic-model/RLS permissions can further constrain data access.
Create a matrix: Identity -> Resource -> Needed action -> Minimum permission -> Owner. Do not solve access by granting Admin everywhere.
8. What you should see / be able to say
A clear diagnosis separating compute availability, item permission, source credentials and data-level security.
Each failure is tested at the control plane where it can actually occur. Professional upgrade: Enterprise automation increasingly uses groups and service
principals rather than personal accounts. Exact tenant/API policies vary; the durable practice is explicit identity/action/scope/owner.
1. Admin workspace role fixes every source-access problem. | 2. Healthy capacity proves data source is reachable. | 3. RLS replaces all
workspace/item permissions. | 4. Use personal credentials for production because they are easiest.
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
For any 'access failed' issue ask four questions: Who is the identity? Which resource? Which action? Which permission/credential controls that action?
Save the genuine attempt before review.
12. Now you do a small version alone
Fresh case: service principal publishes items, analyst builds reports, viewer consumes app, gateway identity reaches SQL Server. Design minimum
No identity receives unexplained broad Admin access; source, workspace and data-level permissions are separate.
14. Teach it back in your own words
Explain why capacity, permission and data credentials are three different reasons a cloud job can succeed or fail.
Attempt first. Changed retry removes one employee and requires group-based access without editing every item manually.
Identity-action-permission matrix + failure diagnosis + explain-back. After saving evidence, continue to CLD3.
Fabric combines many analytics experiences. Memorizing icons does not help you design a solution; you need to know which workload
solves ingestion, engineering, warehouse, real-time or BI consumption problems and how they share OneLake.
Map major Fabric workloads to responsibilities; describe Fabric as end-to-end SaaS analytics; choose the smallest set of workloads needed for
5. New words before we use them
Workload: Fabric experience optimized for a class of analytics tasks. Data Factory: Fabric workload/capabilities for data movement and orchestration.
Real-Time Intelligence: Fabric workload for ingesting/analyzing event and streaming data.
VISUAL/SOURCE ROUTE: Required: current What is Microsoft Fabric overview; optional Power BI Meets Fabric video.
After watching/opening: return to this lesson and reproduce the worked example from your own file/query/report. Save course-task evidence, not a screenshot of the
Shared analytics campus: Fabric workloads are specialized rooms around shared OneLake and common governance. Data Factory
moves/orchestrates, engineering transforms, warehouse serves SQL analytics, real-time handles events and Power BI serves semantic/report
consumption; use only the rooms the solution needs.
Teacher demonstration - do this once with me, then close the example before your fresh task.
Data arrives from CRM/order sources. Data Factory may orchestrate copy/ingestion.
Data Engineering may use Spark/lakehouse transformations when that tool fits the workload.
Data Warehouse may serve governed relational dimensional tables queried with T-SQL.
Real-Time Intelligence is appropriate when operational event streams require real-time analysis; do not add it to a daily batch just because it
Power BI provides semantic/reporting consumption. All required workloads can coexist in Fabric and access shared OneLake data/items
8. What you should see / be able to say
A workload map where every Fabric component has a reason and unnecessary services are omitted.
You design from task -> workload instead of icon -> task. Professional upgrade: Microsoft currently lists Data Engineering, Data Factory, Data Science,
Real-Time Intelligence, Data Warehouse, Databases and Power BI among Fabric experiences. The list can evolve; workload-to-job reasoning is the durable
1. Every solution needs every Fabric workload. | 2. Data Factory = the warehouse. | 3. Power BI Service and Fabric are unrelated platforms. | 4.
Real-Time Intelligence for monthly CSV reporting.
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
Write the verbs: ingest, transform, store/query, stream, model/report. Map one tool only when a verb needs it. Save the genuine attempt before review.
12. Now you do a small version alone
Fresh case: IoT maintenance events + daily ERP finance + executive BI. Choose Fabric workloads for each path and explain integration.
Every chosen workload solves a named problem; no duplicate/unnecessary workload is added.
14. Teach it back in your own words
Explain Fabric to a beginner as one managed analytics platform containing role-specific work areas over shared data.
Attempt first. Changed retry removes streaming need and simplifies the design.
Workload decision map + simplified alternative + explain-back. After saving evidence, continue to CLD4.
CLD4 - OneLake, lakehouse and warehouse concepts
C2-06 taught when a warehouse/lakehouse pattern fits. Here the new question is how Fabric organizes and shares those items over
OneLake and when shortcuts/shared storage can reduce unnecessary data copies.
Explain OneLake tenant-wide logical storage, workspaces/items and shortcuts; place lakehouse/warehouse items in an enterprise Fabric
topology; avoid duplicating C2-06 dimensional-design theory.
5. New words before we use them
OneLake: Fabric's unified logical data lake for the organization. Shortcut: Reference that provides access to data in another supported location without
traditional copy/migration. Item: Fabric object such as lakehouse, warehouse, semantic model or pipeline inside a workspace.
VISUAL/SOURCE ROUTE: Required visual: OneLake overview; optional 'No Walls, Just Data' session.
After watching/opening: return to this lesson and reproduce the worked example from your own file/query/report. Save course-task evidence, not a screenshot of the
One storage estate with multiple serving patterns: OneLake is the tenant-wide logical lake; workspaces organize ownership; shortcuts can reference
supported data without traditional copying; lakehouse favors file/table engineering patterns while warehouse favors governed relational SQL serving.
Teacher demonstration - do this once with me, then close the example before your fresh task.
Central Data Platform workspace owns curated customer/sales data in a Warehouse or Lakehouse depending on workload.
Finance BI workspace consumes governed semantic/reporting assets rather than receiving uncontrolled CSV copies.
Where appropriate, OneLake shortcuts can expose existing data without duplicating it into another lakehouse; still apply ownership/security.
Document which workspace owns the authoritative item and which team only consumes it.
Do not use OneLake to erase governance boundaries: shared storage does not mean every user sees every item.
8. What you should see / be able to say
A Fabric topology with clear data ownership, shared use and minimized unnecessary copies.
OneLake unifies storage access while workspaces/items/security preserve organizational control. Professional upgrade: OneLake currently supports unified
tenant storage and zero-copy/shortcut patterns to supported external sources. Exact shortcut/security capabilities can evolve, so design must be validated
1. OneLake = one giant folder everyone can read. | 2. Shortcut automatically grants access to every consumer. | 3. Duplicate every dataset per
workspace 'for safety'. | 4. Re-teaching warehouse/lakehouse choice without Fabric topology.
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
Start with authoritative owner and consumer. Ask whether data must be copied, referenced or surfaced as a semantic model. Save the genuine attempt
12. Now you do a small version alone
Fresh case: Marketing needs governed Customer 360 from central lakehouse while Finance uses a warehouse and shared certified semantic model.
For each copy/reference, state why it exists; ownership and permissions remain explicit.
14. Teach it back in your own words
Explain OneLake as one organizational data-lake foundation, not one unrestricted spreadsheet folder.
Attempt first. Changed retry adds an external S3/ADLS source and asks whether a shortcut is preferable to copy.
Workspace/item topology + ownership/copy decision + explain-back. After saving evidence, continue to CLD5.
CLD5 - Power BI Service in enterprise environments
Publishing a PBIX is not the same as enterprise delivery. Teams need clear builder and consumer routes, trusted semantic models,
Design workspace collaboration, semantic-model/report ownership, app/direct share choices, content endorsement and consumer access;
separate build surface from polished distribution.
C2-04 DAX15 lifecycle basics and CLD1-4.
5. New words before we use them
App: Packaged Power BI distribution experience published from a workspace to audiences. Semantic model: Governed analytical model consumed by
reports/Excel/other clients. Endorsement: Power BI/Fabric trust signal such as promoted/certified content under organizational policy.
VISUAL/SOURCE ROUTE: Optional PL-300 Manage and Secure video; current Microsoft collaboration docs control behavior.
After watching/opening: return to this lesson and reproduce the worked example from your own file/query/report. Save course-task evidence, not a screenshot of the
Publishing supply chain: builders work in governed workspaces, semantic models define reusable analytical meaning, reports present it, and
apps/direct sharing distribute it to intended audiences. Production delivery also needs ownership, endorsement, refresh, security and support - not just
Teacher demonstration - do this once with me, then close the example before your fresh task.
BI builders collaborate in a controlled workspace. Consumers do not automatically need edit access to the workspace.
Create/use a governed semantic model with documented owner/freshness/security and reports built on it.
Choose app for broad polished distribution; use direct sharing for narrower cases when appropriate. Record licensing/capacity/tenant
Promote/certify trusted content according to organizational governance, rather than letting five teams publish competing 'official revenue'
Define support owner, refresh owner, change notice and consumer path.
8. What you should see / be able to say
An enterprise delivery plan separating building, governed semantic truth, distribution and support.
Workspace collaboration permissions are not confused with consumer distribution. Professional upgrade: Current PL-300 directly measures
creating/configuring workspaces/apps, publishing/updating items, distribution methods, subscriptions/alerts and content endorsement. Tenant/license
constraints must be checked at implementation time.
1. Give all consumers Contributor because app setup is unfamiliar. | 2. Every report owns its own copied semantic model. | 3. Certified means
mathematically correct forever. | 4. No support/change owner after publish.
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
Draw Builders -> Workspace -> Semantic Model -> Report/App -> Consumers. Add owner/security/freshness at the model and support owner at
distribution. Save the genuine attempt before review.
12. Now you do a small version alone
Fresh case: Sales has 6 builders, 40 managers and 600 viewers. Design workspace + semantic model + app/share route.
Builders/consumers get minimum needed access; one authoritative KPI model is identifiable; distribution/support owners are explicit.
14. Teach it back in your own words
Explain why an app can be better than giving hundreds of people workspace access.
Attempt first. Changed retry introduces external guest/partner consumption and requires a policy check rather than assuming it works.
Builder-consumer architecture + distribution matrix + owner/freshness/security notes + explain-back. After saving evidence, continue to CLD6.
Editing production directly makes rollback, testing and impact analysis difficult. Enterprise BI separates development and released
environments and controls who can promote changes.
Design DEV/TEST/PROD workspace separation, deployment ownership, pre-release validation, deployment-pipeline/CI-CD concepts and
rollback/impact checks without pretending every tenant has the same tooling.
CLD5 enterprise Service delivery and C2-04 lifecycle/change impact basics.
5. New words before we use them
Environment: Separated development/testing/production context for items and configuration. Deployment pipeline: Fabric capability that helps manage
content deployment across pipeline stages/workspaces. CI/CD: Practices/tools for controlled integration, testing and delivery of changes.
VISUAL/SOURCE ROUTE: Required current references: Fabric CI/CD overview and deployment-pipeline documentation.
After watching/opening: return to this lesson and reproduce the worked example from your own file/query/report. Save course-task evidence, not a screenshot of the
Guarded conveyor belt: DEV is where change is built, TEST is where behavior/security are proved, and PROD is what consumers rely on. Promotion
moves forward only after explicit checks; a failed control stops the conveyor. Direct production edits weaken traceability, rollback and impact analysis.
Teacher demonstration - do this once with me, then close the example before your fresh task.
Developer changes measure/report in DEV; production content is not edited directly.
Run model/reconciliation/report/security checks in DEV and then controlled TEST/user acceptance as required.
Review impact: downstream reports/apps/refresh/security/config. Record release approver.
Deploy/promote items using the organization's supported method, such as Fabric deployment pipelines and/or Git-integrated CI/CD where
After release, verify PROD refresh/security/KPI smoke checks and define rollback/redeployment path. Pipeline permissions and workspace
8. What you should see / be able to say
A controlled release path with evidence before and after production promotion.
Changes are separated from production consumers until validation/approval is complete. Professional upgrade: Fabric deployment pipelines and broader
CI/CD/Git capabilities evolve. Use current docs at implementation; preserve environment separation, review, validation and rollback as durable controls.
1. DEV and PROD are tabs in one workbook only. | 2. Deployment pipeline automatically tests business correctness. | 3. Contributor can deploy
everywhere without separate pipeline/workspace permissions. | 4. No post-deploy smoke or rollback plan.
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
12. Now you do a small version alone
Fresh case: change Customer Segment logic used by 12 reports. Build DEV/TEST/PROD route and an impact/release checklist.
No production edit occurs before validation; approver, dependencies, post-deploy smoke and rollback are explicit.
14. Teach it back in your own words
Explain deployment pipelines as release control, not a magical correctness checker.
Attempt first. Changed retry introduces a failed TEST validation and asks what must not reach PROD.
Environment map + release checklist + impact analysis + explain-back. After saving evidence, continue to CLD7.
CLD7 - Refresh, gateways and scheduled operations
A report can be perfect at 9 PM and wrong at 9 AM if refresh credentials, gateway mapping or schedules fail. Freshness is an operational
Decide when an on-premises gateway is required; distinguish cloud/on-prem connections; design credentials, refresh cadence, failure
ownership and freshness checks; avoid personal-account dependency.
CLD2 identity, CLD5 Service and C2-04 lifecycle basics.
5. New words before we use them
On-premises data gateway: Software bridge that lets cloud services securely reach supported data sources in a private/on-premises network. Scheduled
refresh: Configured recurring refresh of a semantic model/data source connection. Freshness SLA: Maximum acceptable data age for the business use case.
VISUAL/SOURCE ROUTE: Required visual: Power BI Gateway getting-started video; official gateway/refresh docs control current behavior.
After watching/opening: return to this lesson and reproduce the worked example from your own file/query/report. Save course-task evidence, not a screenshot of the
Delivery route: cloud service -> stored credentials/identity -> gateway when the source is on-premises -> source -> refresh job -> semantic/report
freshness SLA. A green job proves a job completed, not that every required upstream partition was complete or that business data is current.
Teacher demonstration - do this once with me, then close the example before your fresh task.
Classify data source location/connectivity. If Power BI/Fabric cannot reach the on-prem/private source directly, design a gateway/connection
Map all required source connections/credentials; one missing source mapping can make a gateway unavailable for the semantic model.
Choose refresh cadence from business need and source/load constraints-not 'as often as possible'.
Assign technical owner and business freshness owner; use non-personal/team-managed credentials where policy supports it.
After refresh, validate both technical success and business freshness/row/control totals. A successful refresh with stale source data is still a
8. What you should see / be able to say
A refresh runbook with source connectivity, credential/gateway mapping, schedule, owners and post-refresh controls.
Network/credential/schedule/business freshness are tested separately. Professional upgrade: Current Power BI scheduled-refresh guidance separates
gateway connection, credentials and schedule. Exact refresh limits/licensing vary; do not hard-code them into architecture without current verification.
1. Gateway required for every cloud source. | 2. Use analyst's personal password for production refresh. | 3. Refresh succeeded = source data
current. | 4. No owner for expired credential/gateway outage.
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
Trace Source -> Network path -> Credential -> Gateway/connection -> Semantic model -> Schedule -> Freshness validation. Save the genuine attempt
12. Now you do a small version alone
Fresh case: semantic model uses cloud SaaS + on-prem SQL + SharePoint. Decide gateway/credentials and create an 8 AM freshness runbook.
Each source has correct connectivity method; owners and failure escalation exist; business freshness is checked after technical refresh.
14. Teach it back in your own words
Explain why a gateway is about connectivity to a source, not a speed booster.
Attempt first. Changed retry simulates expired SQL credential at 06:00 and requires recovery/escalation.
Connectivity map + refresh schedule/owner matrix + failure runbook + explain-back. After saving evidence, continue to CLD8.
Giving people access is not one checkbox. Workspace roles, item/semantic-model access, row-level security, OneLake/item security and
governance/catalog signals solve different parts of the problem.
Apply least privilege across workspace/item/data layers; use groups; distinguish access control from RLS; add
CLD2 identity, CLD5 Service and C2-04 RLS.
5. New words before we use them
Workspace role: Admin, Member, Contributor or Viewer permission level within a Fabric workspace. Item-level access: Permission granted to a specific
report, semantic model or Fabric item rather than whole workspace. Sensitivity label: Governance/compliance classification applied under organizational
VISUAL/SOURCE ROUTE: Required current references: workspace roles, permission model, OneLake catalog Govern/Purview.
After watching/opening: return to this lesson and reproduce the worked example from your own file/query/report. Save course-task evidence, not a screenshot of the
Building access model: workspace roles grant broad collaboration privileges, item/app permissions shape consumption, and data-level controls such
as RLS narrow what an authorized consumer can see. Least privilege uses groups/service principals and the smallest scope/time needed; governance
adds ownership, lineage, sensitivity and auditability.
Teacher demonstration - do this once with me, then close the example before your fresh task.
Builders belong to appropriate security groups and get only required workspace roles.
Consumers receive app/item/semantic-model access rather than Contributor by convenience.
RLS limits rows inside the model for users who can query it; it does not replace workspace/item permission design.
Use OneLake catalog/endorsement/sensitivity/governance features to improve discovery, trust and policy visibility where the organization
Schedule access review: leavers, role changes, dormant broad access, external users and certified-content owners.
8. What you should see / be able to say
Layered least-privilege design with access owner and recurring review.
Each security/governance control has a separate purpose and ownership. Professional upgrade: Current Fabric workspace roles are
Admin/Member/Contributor/Viewer, while Fabric/Power BI also support item-specific and data-security mechanisms. Current PL-300 directly assesses
workspace/item/semantic-model access, RLS and sensitivity labels.
1. RLS means user can safely be workspace Admin. | 2. Viewer and app audience are identical concepts. | 3. Certified content means anyone
may access it. | 4. Permissions assigned individually forever without group/review strategy.
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
Create columns: identity/group, resource, action, workspace role, item permission, data restriction, approval owner, review date. Save the genuine
12. Now you do a small version alone
Fresh case: Finance builders, regional managers, executives and auditors need different actions/data. Build least-privilege matrix and quarterly review
No persona gets broader access than needed; RLS and item access are not conflated; owner/review date exists.
14. Teach it back in your own words
Explain workspace permission versus RLS using 'can open the building' versus 'which records can you see once inside'.
Attempt first. Changed retry removes a regional manager and adds an external auditor under explicit policy review.
Least-privilege matrix + governance/catalog plan + access-review checklist + explain-back. After saving evidence, continue to CLD9.
Enterprise analytics is not finished when the pipeline/report is published. Someone must detect failures, know the affected consumers,
Use run status/history and monitoring concepts to triage failed refresh/pipeline jobs; distinguish symptom/root cause; design incident evidence,
severity, ownership, recovery and recurrence prevention.
CLD7 refresh operations and C2-05 logging/validation concepts helpful but not required.
5. New words before we use them
Monitoring: Observing operational health, status, history and signals from analytics jobs/items. Incident: Unplanned event that degrades correctness,
freshness, access or availability. Root cause: Underlying condition whose correction prevents or reduces recurrence, not merely the visible symptom.
VISUAL/SOURCE ROUTE: Required current reference: Fabric monitoring hub; optional Learn Live Data Factory pipelines video.
After watching/opening: return to this lesson and reproduce the worked example from your own file/query/report. Save course-task evidence, not a screenshot of the
Smoke alarm plus dependency map: monitoring starts with the visible symptom, then traces the first broken dependency, business impact, responsible
owner, recovery action and downstream validation. A successful pipeline badge is evidence about execution status, not proof that source
completeness, security or freshness is correct.
Teacher demonstration - do this once with me, then close the example before your fresh task.
Detect: report freshness check fails at 08:05. Record incident start, affected KPI/audience and required freshness SLA.
Check monitoring/refresh/job history: determine which job failed and capture exact status/error/time.
Trace dependencies: source availability -> credential/gateway -> ingestion/pipeline -> warehouse/model -> report. Find the first broken stage.
Recover safely: fix/renew/retry from appropriate step, then rerun downstream validation rather than only refreshing the final report.
Close incident with root cause, impact, evidence, owner and prevention action such as alert, credential rotation process, schema contract or
8. What you should see / be able to say
A repeatable incident runbook that connects monitoring signal to affected business output and safe recovery.
You diagnose dependencies from first broken layer instead of randomly clicking Refresh. Professional upgrade: Fabric's Monitor/monitoring hub currently
centralizes job execution health/history. Teams may add alerts/SLAs/ticketing outside Fabric; the course assesses the operational thinking, not one UI.
1. Retry until green without root cause. | 2. Only record screenshot of final report. | 3. No business-impact/severity field. | 4. Fix pipeline but never
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
Use five boxes: Impact -> First failed job -> Dependency cause -> Recovery -> Prevention. Do not skip impact/validation. Save the genuine attempt
12. Now you do a small version alone
Fresh case: nightly pipeline succeeds but semantic-model refresh fails; build incident timeline, root-cause tree and recovery/prevention actions.
Incident record includes status/error/time, affected consumers/KPI, first broken dependency, safe rerun path and prevention owner.
14. Teach it back in your own words
Explain why 'Refresh failed' is a symptom, not automatically the root cause.
Attempt first. Changed retry uses a pipeline that succeeds technically but produces stale source data.
Incident report + dependency tree + recovery validation + prevention action + explain-back. After saving evidence, continue to CLD10.
CLD10 - Analyst - analytics engineer - data engineer collaboration
A senior analyst should not throw vague tickets at engineers or silently rebuild engineering logic in Power BI. Strong teams agree on
ownership, grains, freshness, definitions and failure evidence.
Distinguish typical responsibilities without rigid job-title stereotypes; write usable data contracts/issues/change requests; identify when the
analyst should self-serve, escalate or collaborate.
All C2-07 plus C2-06 lineage/quality and C2-05 reproducibility concepts.
5. New words before we use them
Data contract: Explicit agreement about dataset structure, grain, keys, freshness, quality expectations and ownership. Handoff: Transfer of a
requirement/change/incident with enough evidence for the receiving role to act. Escalation: Raising a problem to the role/team that owns the affected system
VISUAL/SOURCE ROUTE: Book-led; current PL-300 audience profile and Fabric collaboration context support the lesson.
After watching/opening: return to this lesson and reproduce the worked example from your own file/query/report. Save course-task evidence, not a screenshot of the
Contract handoff: the analyst owns the business question, KPI meaning and acceptance evidence; the analytics engineer owns reusable
transformation/semantic contracts; the data engineer owns reliable source ingestion and platform pipelines. Lineage, interfaces, owners and testable
acceptance criteria keep handoffs from becoming guesswork.
Teacher demonstration - do this once with me, then close the example before your fresh task.
Analyst proves impact: Revenue KPI changed after 07:00 refresh; records expected/observed values and affected report/consumers.
Trace lineage to staging table where RegionCode renamed/changed. Do not immediately hard-code a workaround in the report.
Data/analytics engineering owners receive a reproducible issue: source/object, schema diff, grain/key, first failing transformation, sample IDs,
Engineering repairs or intentionally changes upstream contract; analyst validates business semantics and downstream KPI after redeploy.
Team records ownership/prevention: schema-change notification, tests, versioned contract or consumer impact process.
8. What you should see / be able to say
A handoff that another technical role can act on without a meeting just to discover basic facts.
Business impact and technical evidence meet at a shared contract rather than being thrown over a team boundary. Professional upgrade: Current PL-300
audience guidance explicitly expects Power BI analysts to collaborate with analytics engineers and data engineers to identify/acquire data. Exact job
boundaries vary by company; contract/evidence quality is the portable skill.
1. Analyst = dashboards only, engineer = everything technical. | 2. Opening 'data is wrong' ticket with no expected/observed evidence. | 3.
Rebuilding official transformations locally to avoid collaboration. | 4. Engineer owns KPI business definition by default.
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
Use issue template: Business impact -> expected/observed -> dataset/item -> grain/key -> lineage point -> freshness -> evidence -> requested action
-> owner/deadline. Save the genuine attempt before review.
12. Now you do a small version alone
Fresh case: Support SLA dashboard needs a new event field unavailable downstream. Decide which role owns definition, ingestion, transformation,
Every deliverable/decision has one accountable owner; handoff includes reproducible evidence and agreed acceptance check.
14. Teach it back in your own words
Explain analyst, analytics engineer and data engineer collaboration as overlapping responsibilities connected by contracts-not three isolated ladders.
Attempt first. Changed retry is a schema-deprecation notice requiring impact analysis and coordinated migration.
RACI/ownership map + issue/change template + acceptance validation + explain-back. After saving evidence, complete the module mastery checklist
and follow the Gate A / completion route.
Use after the first pass; live UI exposure never replaces reasoning
CLD1 Can you separate tenant/workspace/capacity/items? | CLD2 Is failure compute, identity, credential or data permission? | CLD3 Why
does each Fabric workload exist? | CLD4 Who owns authoritative OneLake items and why copy/shortcut? | CLD5 How do builders and
consumers differ? | CLD6 What prevents an unvalidated change reaching PROD? | CLD7 Does every source have
connectivity/credential/refresh/freshness ownership? | CLD8 Which workspace/item/data/governance control grants or restricts access? |
CLD9 What is the first broken dependency and recovery/prevention? | CLD10 Can another role act on your handoff without rediscovering
Fabric workload added; uncontrolled data copies; consumers
given build roles; direct PROD edits; personal refresh credentials;
gateway misunderstood; RLS treated as all security; incident only

receive required cloud/engineering prerequisites in their own route.

C2_07 Practical Mastery Check - RC4
Closed-book, non-gating diagnostic. Save your first attempt before opening the protected review.
Task
Fresh transfer prompt
1
A source is in an on-premises SQL Server. Draw the minimum refresh dependency chain and identify the component that

A contractor needs one certified report for two weeks. Explain why workspace Contributor is a poor default and propose the

proceeds and state the evidence needed before retry.

semantic definition has changed.

cannot be assumed for all sources.

8
An operations app suddenly shows all regions to regional managers. Give the first three evidence checks and name the
severity/release implication.
9

10

prevention.
Evidence

masteryReview.text:
Course 2A | C2_07 | Astra Parity RC4
Page 1
C2_07 Practical Mastery Check - Protected Review RC4
Open only after a saved genuine Module Test attempt. Use to diagnose, then close it and do a changed retry.
Task
Expected reasoning pattern
1
Cloud service -> stored identity/credentials -> on-premises data gateway -> SQL source -> refresh -> semantic/report. A cloud
SaaS source may not require the on-prem gateway, but credentials/identity and freshness still matter.
2
Granting Contributor exposes broad build privileges. Prefer the narrowest item/app audience/guest route that satisfies the
certified-report need, with explicit owner and expiry/review.
3
Do not promote. The failed security rule is blocking. Repair it, retest in TEST, record PASS evidence and then run the release
checklist again.
4
The job executed successfully. It does not prove the upstream partition was complete/current. Compare source
watermark/partition completeness and business freshness SLA before declaring the report current.
5
Analyst owns KPI/business acceptance; analytics engineer owns transformation/semantic contract; data engineer owns
source ingestion/pipeline reliability. All three record dependency/definition changes and acceptance evidence.
6
On-prem SQL requires the gateway; cloud API/SharePoint do not by default. Each source can have a different expected
availability/freshness, so the report freshness rule must consider all required inputs.
7
DEV builds, TEST validates function/security/impact, PROD serves consumers. Direct PROD editing bypasses repeatable
validation/traceability and complicates rollback.
8
Check audience/RLS group mapping, effective identity/role and last security/deployment change. Broad data exposure is a
security incident; block further release and contain access before normal operation resumes.
9
Workspace role controls broad collaboration capabilities; item/app access narrows which artifacts are consumable; RLS/data
permission narrows which rows/data an authorized consumer sees.
10
A good record separates symptom from root dependency, quantifies affected users/KPIs, assigns owner, records recovery
and proves downstream behavior/freshness/security after recovery; add a prevention/control action.
Changed retry rule
Close this review. Redesign the same controls for a different domain/source mix, including at least one cloud source, one
on-prem source, a failed release control and a permission incident. Save the retry separately. Module Test remains
non-gating.

C2-07 Protected Practice Review
OPEN ONLY AFTER THE MATCHING GENUINE ATTEMPT
Course 2A - C2-07 Protected Learning
Page 1
HOW TO USE
Compare enterprise reasoning and evidence, not UI screenshots. Preserve your original attempt. Close the review before the changed
retry. If a live tenant feature is unavailable, compare the deterministic design/runbook evidence instead.
CRITICAL FAILURES
Admin/Contributor granted to consumers by convenience; tenant/workspace/capacity confused; direct unvalidated PROD editing;
missing gateway/credential/freshness ownership; RLS treated as all security; production access not reviewed; incident repeatedly retried
without root cause/downstream validation; vague engineer handoff.
LIVE-UI RULE
A screenshot of a green Fabric/Power BI page cannot prove architecture mastery. The evidence must state who owns the resource, what
is allowed, what can fail, how it is validated and what happens next.

Course 2A | C2_07 | Astra Parity RC4
Page 2
Page 2 - Expected reasoning and traps
Expected reasoning / diagnostic control
Fleet PROD is a consumer production boundary; Fleet Data Platform PROD is a separate platform-owned production workspace.
The report cannot be certified fresh earlier than every required input satisfies its own availability/freshness rule; Excel Targets is latest at
05:45 if all three are required.
Only OnPremMaintenanceSQL requires the on-premises gateway in this fixture.
The failed Maintenance Status logic change blocks promotion even though the downtime measure passed.
A green pipeline plus low vehicle count proves execution status and business completeness are different controls.
fleet-vendor should not receive broad workspace build rights for a temporary single-report need.
Common failure patterns
Looks plausible
Why it fails
Green refresh/pipeline means data is correct
Execution state does not prove upstream completeness, correct security or business
freshness.
Give broad workspace role because it is
easier
It violates least privilege and expands build/share/admin capability beyond the business
need.
Promote because most tests passed
A designated blocking security/logic control must pass before TEST -> PROD
promotion.
Use one freshness timestamp for all sources
Cloud/on-prem/stream/reference sources have different availability and dependencies.
Fix symptom and close incident
Recovery is incomplete until downstream access/freshness/business behavior is
validated.

Required evidence

Name the exact failed competency: architecture boundary, permission scope, gateway/credential,
freshness, release gate or incident reasoning.
2. Repair
Revisit only the named lesson/practice control. Write one corrected decision and why the previous decision
was unsafe/incomplete.
3. Close review
Do not keep the worked review visible during the reassessment.
4. Changed fresh retry
Solve a new domain/source/persona/release/incident case. Fresh B/C evidence must not reuse the prior
Gate answer.
5. Save evidence
Store retry decision table/diagram, assumptions, validation checks, incident/release result and own-words
explanation as a new artifact.
Pass standard
The learner can make the new decisions without the review open, justify least privilege and environment boundaries,
distinguish execution from business correctness, block unsafe promotion, and explain what evidence would prove recovery.
